A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Galileo. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title, extensive rewriting, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream evaluations, representation measurements, computational comparisons, and method and modality ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds targeted batch-size, location-input, loss-configuration, and patch-size results.

M1.justification: The channel-group ViT, EMA targets, modality-dependent target depths, structured and random masking, separate predictors, and final dual-PatchDisc objective are retained. AllDisc is renamed PatchDiscB. The rewritten explanation and problematic new loss formula do not establish an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both use the same 127,155-instance multimodal pretraining dataset and downstream coverage: six GeoBench tasks, MADOS, Sen1Floods11, PASTIS, Breizhcrops, and CropHarvest. The additional ablations vary configurations within this coverage.

E2.justification: The comparator sets and baseline architectures in corresponding image and pixel-time-series evaluations are unchanged. DOFA becomes DOFA-v1 without changed participation or benchmark scores; AllDisc becomes PatchDiscB in the ablations.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 changes the reported minibatch from 128 to 32 while retaining effective batch size 512 and four repetitions. Appendix B.1 changes the clustering class features from WorldCereal to WorldCover. New evaluations include minibatch size 16 and MADOS patch size 2. These are reported setting changes and additions, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds batch-size sensitivity in Table 10, location removal in Table 11, MADOS patch-size sensitivity in Table 13, and a full-target-context PatchDiscB/PatchDisc configuration in Table 9. These extend existing design and sensitivity analyses without replacing the main ablation framework.

E5.justification: Both specify five linear-probe runs and averaging in Appendix C.3, with no added seed lists, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new 100% versus 63% success statement summarizes different ablation configurations, rather than reporting new repeated-seed uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The principal benchmark scores and rankings are unchanged, including the full appendix tables. New results accompany the added ablations; for example, v2 Table 13 reports Galileo-Base MADOS performance of 68.4 at patch size 2 versus the retained 67.6 at patch size 4. Table 2 expresses existing similarities as their complements. The new Table 13 also reports 41.5 for Nano at 20% training and patch size 4, conflicting with 41.4 in retained Table 17.

T1.justification: v2 adds an explicit within-input PatchDisc formula in Section 2.2.4. Its printed expression omits the negative sign and uses matching-pair indices throughout the denominator, conflicting with the intended contrastive objective and the retained Appendix A.1.1 formulation. The cross-batch definition otherwise survives under its new name; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: Both claim flexible multimodal and multiscale Galileo models, complementary global/local self-supervision, and strong performance against image and pixel-time-series specialists. v2 foregrounds the single-generalist interpretation and eleven benchmarks, but these describe the existing contribution and evaluation scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds a possible positional-embedding shortcut explanation for global-only PatchDisc failure and explains why shallow targets avoid that shortcut. The conclusion explicitly states that applying local/global self-supervision beyond remote sensing requires further investigation, qualifying v1's broader hoped-for relevance.

D1.justification: v2 revises the minibatch and sampling-feature descriptions and identifies 32 as the memory-limited default for the batch-size experiment. It removes v1's explicit patch-dependent positional-embedding interpolation rule. Hardware, training-cost tables, hyperparameter sweeps, and code/data access remain unchanged. The revised description leaves how 32 instances repeated four times yields effective batch size 512 unexplained.

R1.justification: The literature discussion is substantially recast around modality and temporal coverage and Galileo's relationship to latent prediction. v2 removes the discussion justifying exclusion of RGB-only, unavailable-weight, and superseded models, along with references such as SkySense, OmniSat, and SatViT. It adds contextual works including Chen et al. (2021), ImageNet, Kinetics, and Rao et al. (2020), and expands its positioning against AnySat.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method exposition, and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten. Section 2 now introduces intuition followed by tokenization, masking, encoding, and losses before describing the dataset. Terminology changes include AllDisc to PatchDiscB, and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds an application overview as Figure 1 and substantially redraws the training diagram in Figure 2. The original SSL comparison moves to Figure 5, and the appendix sampling map moves into the main text as Figure 3. New sensitivity tables, revised captions and metric headers, and changed ablation highlighting substantially alter presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 provides clearer method organization and useful additional sensitivity evidence while retaining the main benchmark results. However, it introduces a mathematically inconsistent PatchDisc formula and an unexplained effective-batch calculation, and removes positional-scaling details. These regressions affect reproducibility of the central method. The presentation and evidential gains coexist with technical ambiguities that the PDFs do not resolve, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
